data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A bounded harness produces better surviving conjectures because it enforces a selection pressure analogous to natural selection, filtering out high-variance, low-coherence outputs that a single model call would accept as final.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the harness's filtering criteria are misaligned with truth (e.g., preferring elegant but false mechanisms), the surviving conjectures will be systematically worse than a random single call.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the model's internal distribution is already peaked sharply around the correct answer, the overhead of the harness provides negligible improvement.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the problem space is non-stationary and changes faster than the harness iteration cycle, the 'surviving' conjectures become obsolete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Iterative rejection sampling: The harness acts as a filter function H(C) -> {0,1} applied to a stream of candidate conjectures C generated by the model. By only allowing conjectures that satisfy specific structural constraints (e.g., causal mechanism presence) to 'survive' to the next state, the system accumulates quality over time, whereas a single call relies entirely on the probability mass of the first token sequence.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
